title: Alternative approaches to sentencing
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T08:14:05Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank point teaches circle sentencing and restorative justice in NSW Year 12, not the Drug Court, Koori Court or diversion programs that target the causes of offending, so no existing point teaches the same idea at this depth.

draft.title: Alternative approaches to sentencing
card: Some offending has causes such as drug dependence, or a link to a person's community. Alternative approaches try to deal with these causes, so the offender is less likely to offend again.
Drug Court
a Victorian court for some offenders whose offending is linked to drug use. It can order treatment and regular testing, with close supervision by the court.
Koori Court
a Victorian court for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander offenders who plead guilty. Elders and respected persons take part in the hearing, so the sentence is more culturally appropriate.
Diversion program
a way to deal with an offence without a full court process. The accused may agree to conditions, such as counselling or an apology, and the case can then be dealt with without a conviction.
draft.remember: Alternative approaches aim at the causes of offending, to reduce reoffending.

a.q: What do the Drug Court, the Koori Court and diversion programs have in common?
opts: They try to deal with the causes of offending
They aim to give the offender the longest sentence
They only apply to people who plead not guilty
They replace the need for any sanction at all
a.why: Each approach looks at why the person offended, such as drug use or a link to community, and tries to reduce reoffending. They do not aim for longer sentences, and the Koori Court needs a guilty plea.
a.clue: Think about what each approach tries to change in the offender's life.

b.q: Jack has been charged with theft. His offending is linked to heroin dependence. Which approach is most suited to the cause of his offending?
opts: The Drug Court, with treatment and court supervision
The Koori Court, with Elders taking part in the hearing
A larger fine, to increase the penalty for him
A longer prison term, to keep him away from drugs
b.why: The Drug Court is for offending linked to drug use and can order treatment with close supervision. The Koori Court is for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander offenders, and the card gives no sign that Jack is one. A fine or prison would not deal with the dependence.
b.clue: Match the approach to the cause of Jack's offending.

a.best: They try to deal with the causes of offending

b.best: The Drug Court, with treatment and court supervision

problems.detail: 'Some offending has causes such as ... a link to a person's community' is confusing and could suggest that belonging to a community, read here as an Aboriginal community, causes offending. The Koori Court aims to make sentencing culturally appropriate and to reconnect offenders with community and culture. The why for (a) repeats this framing.
The Victorian Drug Court deals with offending linked to drug or alcohol dependence. The card says only 'drug use', which is incomplete.

check.summary: Both answers are clear and correct. The card's phrase 'a link to a person's community' as a cause of offending is confusing and risks a harmful reading about Aboriginal communities, so it should be reworded. The Drug Court description should also mention alcohol.
